title: SWE-1.6: MODEL UX
lede: Spring 2026. The training runs got two orders of magnitude more compute, and Cognition spent the surplus on something unusual: manners. SWE-1.6 was post-trained to jointly optimize intelligence and 'model UX' — how the model feels to work with, not just what it scores.
body:
h2. THE PREVIEW

p. Cognition broke its own tradition and published %(ok)mid-run results%. The SWE-1.6 Preview checkpoint — post-trained from the same base as SWE-1.5 — was already *+11% on SWE-Bench Pro* over its predecessor while running at the same 950 tok/s. The stated reason for the peek: get real users on the checkpoint early and tune behavior with feedback, not vibes.

p. The eval table in that post is a time capsule of the frontier in early 2026: Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.3-Codex and Codex-Spark, GLM-5, Kimi K2.5, Composer-1.5 — every model run through the same three harnesses (Claude Code, Cascade, Devin) where vendors hadn't reported numbers.

h2. GENERALLY AVAILABLE

p. April 2026: SWE-1.6 shipped to everyone in Windsurf with a pricing stunt — %(hl)free for three months%. Two serving paths:

* %(cyan)Fireworks% — the free tier at ~200 tok/s.
* %(amber)Cerebras% — the paid tier at 950 tok/s, sold as %(ok)SWE-1.6 Fast%: same intelligence, unmatched speed.

h2. WHAT 'MODEL UX' MEANT

* Smoother turn-taking — fewer stalls, fewer degenerate loops, better pacing on long tasks.
* Trained for the agent experience end-to-end rather than benchmark-pinned.
* A signal that the frontier was moving past raw score: SWE-Bench Pro had already displaced SWE-Bench as the eval that mattered — harder, less contaminated, longer-horizon.

bq. SWE-1.6 is optimized for both intelligence and model UX — trained to make the model feel smoother to use, in addition to raw intelligence. %(dim)— Cognition, April 2026%
